newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Gold-Fall always in cards - dealers.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Gold-Fall always in cards - dealers.

text.p: While concerns over planned Swiss National Bank (SNB) gold sales have been linked to a dramatic fall in gold prices on Wednesday, dealers here said the price roll back was always in the cards.
"Gold was perceived as being oversold and due for a correction before the Swiss announcement," one dealer said.
The market interpreted plans by the SNB to revalue about 20 percent of its 2,600 tonnes of gold reserves, in part to create a humanitarian fund, as a willingness on the bank's part to dump gold.
This pushed COMEX April gold US$6.10 lower to $354.50 an ounce on Wednesday. In intraday trading the price had slipped as low as $352.40 an ounce.
Bullion on Wednesday ended quoted $352.70-$353.20 an ounce.
"From what we can tell, what's occurred is an over- reaction," Mark Freemantle, senior bullion dealer for Rothschild Australia Ltd said.
Another dealer said gold was destined to come under pressure after soaring in recent weeks, to what one called "unrealistic heights," given prevailing investor sentiment for the metal.
"Gold is competing in a non-inflationary environment, which makes it less attractive to other investments," said Stewart Murray, analyst for Gold Fields Mineral Services Ltd.
Dealers said profit-takers were already waiting in the wings to pounce on gold as prices made their way higher, partly on the tail of firmer platinum prices.
"Gold was going up and everyone was wating for signs of peak," one said.
A technical support point widely marked at US$350 an ounce should lend some support to the price in European and U.S. trading, the dealer said.
But one cautioned any sustained dip below $350 an ounce could trigger a wider sell off.
The dealers were attending the Australian Gold Conference here.
